NEGOTIATED.src: LM_HG201 prior-day, 2026-11-17 slaughter (USDA AMS 2511 + lsddhps, agreeing). low/high are the report's Lowest/Highest Net Lot, the only dispersion LM_HG201 publishes. roll5 is the mean of the five most recent PUBLISHED negotiated base prices held here (Nov 6, 9, 10, 16, 17 = 43.54); Nov 11-13 were never captured by earlier runs, so this spans Nov 6-17 rather than five consecutive sessions. || 2026-11-19 RUN: an aggregator rendering of the LM_HG201 prior-day report published 2026-11-19 (covering the 2026-11-18 slaughter) was found, but it could NOT be corroborated. The only independent route to that report, the AMS lsddhps.pdf endpoint, was serving a stale file printed 2026-10-23. The aggregator page also contradicted itself (three head counts printed two different ways) and its stated national change of -0.81 is inconsistent with its own level against the 2026-11-17 figures held here. Per RUNBOOK, the figure is treated as unverified: the old value and its OLD asof date are kept and the gate is left to flag it. Nothing was interpolated or carried forward under today's date.

CUTOUT.src: LM_PK602 afternoon (FOB plant). 2026-11-18 PM cutout 69.48 (+1.04 from 68.44) RE-CONFIRMED this session by two independent sources: the ThePigSite CME wire dated 2026-11-19 ("priced pork carcasses on Wednesday afternoon at $69.48 per hundredweight ... up $1.04 from $68.44 on Tuesday") and Barchart ("back up $1.04 in the Wednesday PM report, at $69.48"). The 2026-11-19 PM cutout could NOT be obtained: the AMS mnreports endpoints ams_2498.pdf and lsddhps.pdf were fetched and found to be serving STALE cached files printed 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-23 respectively, and no wire covering the 2026-11-19 afternoon report had published by run time. Value and asof therefore held at 2026-11-18 rather than carried forward with today's date. One aggregator was seen publishing a pork cutout of $182.06; that is the known column-summing mis-parse and was discarded.

FEED.src: CBOT 2026-11-19 settlements. Dec 26 corn 4.39, +0.035, confirmed by TWO independent sources agreeing to the quarter-cent: Pro Farmer 'After the Bell' dated 2026-11-19 ("December corn rose 3 1/2 cents to $4.39") and the GX94 closing table of 2026-11-19 ("CORN DEC 4.39 up 3 1/2"). Dec 26 soybean meal 332.30, -3.60, is SINGLE-SOURCED from the same Pro Farmer piece ("December soybean meal lost $3.60 to $332.30"); no second source was reachable, so it is labelled here rather than presented as cross-checked. The corn agreement validates that article for this session. Priors (corn 4.355, meal 335.90) are back-calculated from the published daily changes and are NOT added to the series as if published; the series jumps from 2026-11-16 to 2026-11-19 because the 2026-11-17 and 2026-11-18 closes were not obtained.

EXPORTS.src: USDA FAS Weekly Export Sales, Weekly Highlights report, read direct from apps.fas.usda.gov. The document states it covers the period 2026-10-30 to 2026-11-05 and its daily-reporting table is 'For Period Ending November 5, 2026', so asof is the 2026-11-05 week ending - NOT today. Primary-source single read; no second source was reachable. This replaces a block whose asof was the unparseable string 'mid-October 2026', which the freshness gate was scoring as MISSING. A newer FAS release covering the week ending 2026-11-12 may exist; its page could not be fetched this session, so the verified 2026-11-05 figures are used and the gate still flags the block as stale. Percentage changes are as FAS prints them, rounded to whole numbers.

COT.pct_rank_note: Managed money net short (futures only) widened to 62,236 contracts from 59,072, a fifth straight weekly build and the largest in the disaggregated series. On a futures-and-options basis the net short is 51,084, which one COT analysis calls the largest since the series began in June 2006. Futures open interest 311,751; futures-and-options open interest 481,857, up 4,754 on the week. Release was pushed from Friday 2026-11-13 to Monday 2026-11-16 by a federal holiday. cme_index below is still the 2026-11-03 reading and carries its own date.

FUTURES.src: Dec 26 is the 2026-11-19 CME settlement: 52.425, +1.075, confirmed by TWO independent sources that agree to the quarter-cent - Pro Farmer 'After the Bell' dated 2026-11-19 ("December lean hog futures rose $1.075 to $52.425") and the GX94 closing commodity table published 2026-11-19 14:18 ("LEAN HOGS DEC 52.42 up 1.07"). It chains exactly to the 2026-11-18 settlement of 51.35. Feb 27 is the 2026-11-19 settlement 58.05 (+0.90) from the GX94 close table; single-sourced, but it chains exactly to the 2026-11-18 Feb settlement of 57.150, which two independent sources printed directly (ThePigSite CME wire dated 2026-11-19 and Barchart 'Hogs Post New Contract Lows on Wednesday'). Apr 27 could NOT be verified for 2026-11-19: no source reached today printed it. Apr 27 is therefore held at its 2026-11-18 settlement of 65.15 (Barchart, -0.375, chaining exactly to the 2026-11-17 settlement of 65.525 that the same source printed directly) and is flagged with stale_asof. No curve snapshot was added for 2026-11-19 because only two of the nine contract months could be verified. Each contract keeps its own history; nothing is spliced across the October roll.

LH_INDEX.note: 56.86 carries an EXPLICIT publication date this session: Barchart, "The CME Lean Hog Index was down 30 cents on November 16 at $56.86". Corroborated by the ThePigSite CME wire dated 2026-11-19 quoting the index "last quoted at 56.86 cents per pound, its lowest value since August 2020", and it chains exactly (-0.30) to the 57.16 previously held. That chain also retroactively validates the earlier DERIVED dating of 57.16 to 2026-11-13 from the standard two-business-day publication lag. The 2026-11-17 index value has not published yet.
